Why Skills? Frank Kilcommins & Erik Wilde: Agent Skills: Introduction

(3) Without Skills: Every Session Starts from Scratch

What you want What actually happens
  • Specific task or goal orientated help in every session
  • Knowledge already loaded
  • Same methodology across teammates
  • Update the approach once, syndicate everywhere
  • Re-explain context at the start of every conversation
  • Same question, very different answers each run
  • Knowledge stays with whoever wrote the best prompt
  • Model updates significantly change behaviour
  • The LLM is capable, but context management is challenging

What Skills Are and How They Work Frank Kilcommins & Erik Wilde: Agent Skills: Introduction

(5) A Skill: Teach Once, Benefit Every Time

  • Structured, reusable instructions packaged as a simple folder
  • Loaded into the agent's context window when relevant - shapes how it thinks and acts
  • Explicit scope: does one thing, with some guardrails, in a defined way
  • Versionable artifact like code) - reviewed, shared, and reused across sessions and agents

The benefit: instead of re-prompting your process in every conversation, you encode it once and the agent applies it consistently.

Warning: model updates can impact the behavior of skills.



What Skills Are and How They Work Frank Kilcommins & Erik Wilde: Agent Skills: Introduction

(6) Anatomy of a Skill

A skill is a folder. The only required file is SKILL.md: 

your-skill-name/
├── SKILL.md        # Required: YAML frontmatter + body instructions
├── scripts/        # Optional: executable code (Python, Bash, etc.)
├── references/     # Optional: documentation loaded as needed
└── assets/         # Optional: templates, examples, output formats

The YAML frontmatter is the trigger. It tells the agent when to activate the skill: 

---
name: your-skill-name
description: >
  What the skill does. Use when the user asks to [specific phrases].
---
# Instructions
Step 1: ...
Step 2: ...


What Skills Are and How They Work Frank Kilcommins & Erik Wilde: Agent Skills: Introduction

(7) How an Agent Uses a Skill: Progressive Disclosure

Skills use a three-level loading system that keeps token usage low:

Level What When loaded
1. Frontmatter Name and trigger description Always - present in every session
2. SKILL.md body Full instructions and constraints When the task matches the skill
3. Linked files Scripts, reference docs, assets On demand, as needed during execution
  • The skill shapes how the agent thinks about the task. It does not replace the LLM's judgment, it just guides it


What Skills Are and How They Work Frank Kilcommins & Erik Wilde: Agent Skills: Introduction

(8) Skill vs. Plain Prompt

Plain Prompt Agent Skill
  • Ephemeral - lost at end of session
  • Re-typed or copy-pasted each time
  • Results vary with who wrote it
  • No versioning, no review process
  • Knowledge silos with individuals
  • Persistent - available in every session
  • Loads automatically when triggered
  • Consistent - same instructions every run
  • Versionable artifact like code - reviewable, auditable, testable
  • Team-wide - one update benefits everyone
